---
# [Bio181L_App_TE.qmd] =================================================
# Tiny Earth Project - Bio 181 Lab (BYU-Idaho)
#
# This is a Quarto "Shiny document": a .qmd file whose `server: shiny`
# setting below turns it into a live web app. Every visitor gets their
# OWN independent session, so many students can use the app at the same
# time.
#
# HOW TO RUN LOCALLY (RStudio)
#   1. Install once:
#        install.packages(c("tidyverse", "shiny", "DT",
#                           "quarto", "rmarkdown"))
#      (scales comes with the tidyverse install.)
#      (Quarto itself ships with recent RStudio versions.)
#   2. Open this file and click "Run Document" (or run
#        quarto::quarto_serve("Bio181L_App_TE.qmd")  in the Console).
#   3. The "Data" folder (made by the Data_Clean script) must sit in the
#      same folder as this file.
#
# HOW TO PUT IT ON THE WEB (so students only need a link)
#   A Shiny document needs a computer running R behind it, so it cannot
#   be hosted as a plain web page (e.g. GitHub Pages). Use a Shiny host
#   such as shinyapps.io (free tier available) or Posit Connect. From
#   RStudio, install `rsconnect`, link your shinyapps.io account, then
#   publish this file together with the whole "Data" folder.
# ======================================================================

# [MAP OF THIS FILE] ===================================================
# Press Ctrl+F / Cmd+F and search the tag, e.g. [D4]
#   [A] YAML settings (this block) ....... page title, layout, turns the document into a Shiny app
#   [B] STYLE SHEET (CSS) ................ colours, layout, buttons, tables, print rules
#         [B1] colour palette   [B2] banner   [B3] viewer layout   [B4] buttons
#         [B5] collapsible sections   [B6] variable picker   [B7] results page
#         [B8] data tables   [B9] print and small screens
#   [C] JAVASCRIPT ....................... tePick(): the Response / Explanatory checkboxes
#   [D0] PACKAGES (R, runs once) ......... every library() the app uses, in its own chunk
#   [D] SETUP (R, runs once) ............. loading data, helpers, statistics
#         [D1] settings   [D2] find the tables   [D3] order and names
#         [D4] load and cache a table  [D5] variable descriptions
#         [D6] variable types and which test fits   [D7] formatting, table and graph helpers
#         [D8] DESIGNER SECTION: ANOVA, regression, chi-squared, test explanations
#         [D9] helpers that build pieces of the page
#   [E] PAGE SHELL (R, built once) ....... banner + an empty "page" for the server to fill
#   [F] SERVER (R, runs for each visitor)  everything that reacts to clicks
#         [F1] app state   [F2] which page shows   [F3] left panel
#         [F4] picker status and Analyse button   [F5] right panel (tables)
#         [F6] click handlers   [F7] Background window   [F8] results page
#         [F9] Learn More window
#
# HOW A CLICK TRAVELS:  a button or link sends a value to R (input$...)  ->  an
# observeEvent() in [F6] updates the visitor's state rv$...  ->  every renderUI()
# that reads rv$... redraws itself  ->  the visitor sees the new screen.
# ======================================================================

# [A. YAML settings] ===================================================
# Page title, layout, and the line that turns this document into a
# Shiny app.
# ======================================================================
pagetitle: "Tiny Earth Project - Bio 181 Lab (BYU-I)"  # page title shown in the browser tab
format:                   # output is an HTML page (a Shiny document = HTML page + a live R process)
  html:
    page-layout: custom   # no Quarto sidebar or margins; the app controls its own layout (see [B])
    toc: false            # no table of contents in the page
execute:                  # code chunks run, but their code, warnings and messages are hidden
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
server: shiny             # makes the document a live Shiny app (needs R running behind it)
---

```{=html}
<!-- [B. STYLE SHEET (CSS)] =============================================
     Clean, professional sea-green + cyan theme. All colours are defined
     once below so they are easy to change.
     ================================================================ -->
<style>
  /* [B1. Colour palette] ==============================================
     Each colour is defined once here and used below as var(--name).
     Change a colour here and it changes everywhere.
       body                           page background and default text
                                      colour
       #quarto-content, main.content  remove Quarto's default page-width
                                      limit so the app uses the whole
                                      window
     ================================================================ */
  :root {
    --sea:        #2E8B57;   /* sea green (primary)            */
    --sea-dark:   #1B5E4B;   /* deep sea green (headings)      */
    --cyan:       #00ACC1;   /* cyan (secondary)               */
    --cyan-light: #E0F7FA;   /* pale cyan (backgrounds)        */
    --mint:       #EAF6F0;   /* pale sea green (backgrounds)   */
    --grey:       #5F7470;
  }
  body                 { background: #F4FAF8; color: #25403A; }
  #quarto-content, main.content { max-width: 100% !important; padding: 0 14px 20px 14px !important; }

  /* [B2. Banner at the very top] ======================================
       .te-banner     green-to-cyan gradient bar across the top of the
                      page
       .te-banner h1  banner title
       .te-banner p   the line of text under the title
     ================================================================ */
  .te-banner { background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sea), var(--cyan)); color: #fff;
               padding: 14px 22px; border-radius: 0 0 12px 12px; margin: 0 -14px 14px -14px; }
  .te-banner h1 { font-size: 1.45rem; margin: 0; font-weight: 700; color: #fff; }
  .te-banner p  { margin: 2px 0 0 0; opacity: .92; font-size: .9rem; }

  /* [B3. Viewer layout: selector (left) + table (right)] ==============
       .app-grid         two-column grid: a 310px selector on the left,
                         the table fills the rest on the right
       .panel-card       the white rounded 'card' that every panel sits on
       .left-card        left card: fixed height, children stacked
                         top-to-bottom so the buttons stay at the bottom
       .selector-scroll  middle of the left card: takes the spare space
                         and scrolls when the list is long
       .sel-title        bold heading at the top of a panel
       .sel-head         small uppercase section heading (Individual /
                         Combined)
       .te-item          one clickable table name in the selector;
                         .active marks the selected table
       .hint             small grey helper text
       .vtype            small grey '(Quantitative)' tag shown after a
                         variable name
       .viewer-head      title row above the Table Viewer / Variable
                         Directory
       .table-foot       line of text under the table (row and column
                         counts)
     ================================================================ */
  .app-grid  { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 310px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 14px; }
  .panel-card { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #CDE7DF; border-radius: 10px; padding: 14px;
                box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(27,94,75,.08); }
  .left-card  { display: flex; flex-direction: column; height: 80vh; }
  .selector-scroll { flex: 1 1 auto; overflow-y: auto; margin: 10px 0; padding-right: 4px; }
  .sel-title  { font-weight: 700; color: var(--sea-dark); font-size: 1.05rem; margin-bottom: 6px; }
  .sel-head   { font-size: .75rem; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 700;
                color: var(--cyan); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); margin: 12px 0 4px; padding-bottom: 2px; }
  .te-item    { display: block; padding: 5px 10px; margin: 1px 0; border-radius: 6px; color: var(--sea-dark);
                text-decoration: none !important; font-size: .93rem; }
  .te-item:hover  { background: var(--cyan-light); }
  .te-item.active { background: var(--sea); color: #fff !important; font-weight: 600; }
  .hint       { color: var(--grey); font-size: .88rem; margin: 2px 0 6px; }
  .vtype      { color: var(--grey); font-size: .8rem; margin-left: 6px; }
  .viewer-head { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; justify-content: space-between; align-items: baseline;
                 border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); margin-bottom: 10px; padding-bottom: 4px; }
  .viewer-head h3 { margin: 0; color: var(--sea-dark); font-size: 1.2rem; }
  .viewer-head .current { color: var(--grey); font-size: .9rem; }
  .table-foot { color: var(--grey); font-size: .85rem; margin-top: 6px; }

  /* [B4. Buttons] =====================================================
       .btn-te            main green button style; every button in the
                          app starts from this
       .btn-cyan          cyan variant of the button
       .btn-outline       white outlined variant, used for secondary
                          actions (Back, Description)
       .btn-wide          makes a button fill the full width of its panel
       .btn-te[disabled]  greyed-out look for a disabled button (Analyse
                          before a valid pair is chosen)
       .btn-glow          glowing cyan look for the Analyse button once a
                          valid pair is chosen
       .btn-row           a row of buttons that share the width evenly
                          (Description + Run Analysis, Back + Analyse)
     ================================================================ */
  .btn-te        { background: var(--sea); color: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--sea); border-radius: 8px;
                   font-weight: 600; padding: 7px 16px; }
  .btn-te:hover  { background: #247549; color: #fff; }
  .btn-cyan      { background: var(--cyan); border-color: var(--cyan); }
  .btn-cyan:hover{ background: #0090a3; }
  .btn-outline   { background: #fff; color: var(--sea-dark); border: 1px solid var(--sea); }
  .btn-outline:hover { background: var(--mint); color: var(--sea-dark); }
  .btn-wide      { width: 100%; }
  .btn-te[disabled] { background: #D5DFDC; border-color: #D5DFDC; color: #8A9A96; cursor: not-allowed; }
  .btn-glow      { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,172,193,.25), 0 0 14px rgba(0,172,193,.85);
                   background: var(--cyan); border-color: var(--cyan); }
  .btn-row       { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; }
  .btn-row .btn  { flex: 1; }
  .btn-row > *   { flex: 1; }                 /* Back and Analyse share the row evenly */
  .btn-row .shiny-html-output .btn { width: 100%; }

  /* [B5. Collapsible selector sections (<details> / <summary>)] =======
     The heading is clickable; the browser's default triangle is hidden.
     We draw our own arrow instead; it turns 90 degrees when the section
     is open.
     ================================================================ */
  details.sel-details > summary.sel-head { cursor: pointer; list-style: none; }
  details.sel-details > summary.sel-head::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; }
  details.sel-details > summary.sel-head::before { content: "\25B8"; display: inline-block; width: 1em;
                                                    transition: transform .15s; }
  details.sel-details[open] > summary.sel-head::before { transform: rotate(90deg); }

  /* [B6. Variable picker: name + Response box + Explanatory box] ======
       .pick-head, .pick-row  header and every row share one 3-column
                              grid (name, Response, Explanatory) so the
                              checkboxes line up
       .pick-head             column headings stay visible (sticky)
                              while the variable list scrolls underneath
       .pick-row              one variable row in the picker (highlights
                              on hover)
       input.pick-resp        Response checkboxes are sea green
       input.pick-expl        Explanatory checkboxes are cyan
     ================================================================ */
  .pick-head, .pick-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 64px 64px; gap: 4px; align-items: center; }
  .pick-head  { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 1; background: #fff; padding: 2px 4px 5px;
                border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); font-size: .78rem; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; }
  .pick-head span:first-child { text-align: left; color: var(--sea-dark); }
  .pick-head .h-resp { color: var(--sea); }
  .pick-head .h-expl { color: var(--cyan); }
  .pick-row   { padding: 3px 4px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: .93rem; }
  .pick-row:hover { background: var(--cyan-light); }
  .pick-name  { overflow-wrap: anywhere; color: var(--sea-dark); }
  .pick-row input { justify-self: center; width: 17px; height: 17px; cursor: pointer; }
  .pick-row input.pick-resp { accent-color: var(--sea); }
  .pick-row input.pick-expl { accent-color: var(--cyan); }

  /* [B7. Results page] ================================================
       .results-bar            top bar of the results page (Back on the
                               left; Learn More and Save PDF on the right)
       .results-page h2        test title at the top of the results
       .sec-title              section headings on the results page
                               (Graph, Numerical Summary, ...)
       .tbl-wrap               wrapper that lets a wide table scroll
                               sideways instead of stretching the page
       .te-table               style for the summary and test tables
                               built by html_table()
       .formula                shaded boxes used for equations and
                               hypotheses
       .concl                  cyan box for written conclusions and
                               warnings
       .note                   small italic grey notes
       ...validation           friendly box for the message shown when a
                               test cannot run (replaces Shiny's faint
                               grey text)
       .more-toggle            space above the View More on Test button
       .more-body              the test details are hidden until the
                               button adds the class 'open' to .more
       .diag-row               diagnostic plots sit side by side and wrap
                               onto the next line on narrow screens
       .shiny-plot-output img  never let a plot be wider than the page
     ================================================================ */
  .results-bar  { display: flex; gap: 10px; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 8px; }
  .results-bar .spacer { flex: 1; }
  .results-page h2   { color: var(--sea-dark); margin: 6px 0 2px; }
  .sec-title    { color: var(--sea-dark); border-bottom: 2px solid var(--cyan-light); padding-bottom: 3px;
                  margin: 22px 0 10px; font-size: 1.15rem; }
  .tbl-wrap     { overflow-x: auto; margin: 6px 0 14px; }

  .more-toggle  { margin-top: 22px; }
  .more-body    { display: none; }

  .shiny-plot-output img { max-width: 100%; height: auto !important; }

  /* [B8. DataTable touches] ===========================================
       table.dataTable thead th  cyan header cells in the data tables

  table.dataTable thead th { background: var(--cyan-light); color: var(--sea-dark); }

  /* [B9. Print ("Save PDF") and small-screen rules] ===================

  @media print {
```
