```{=html}
</style>

<!-- [C. JAVASCRIPT] ====================================================
     One small function, tePick(), that controls the Response /
     Explanatory checkboxes in the variable picker.
     ================================================================ -->
<script>
  // [tePick()] =======================================================
  // Called by every checkbox in the variable picker (see pick_row() in
  // the setup code).
  //  - only ONE box may be ticked in each column (Response / Explanatory)
  //  - one variable cannot be both Response and Explanatory
  // It then tells the server which variable is in each column
  // (input$sel_pair).
  // ==================================================================
  function tePick(col, box) {
    var other = (col === 'resp') ? 'expl' : 'resp';  // the opposite column to this box's column

    // [Untick] =======================================================
    // Untick every other box in this column, so only one is ticked per
    // column. If this variable is ticked in the other column too, untick
    // it there (a variable cannot be both).
    // ================================================================
    document.querySelectorAll('input.pick-' + col).forEach(function (b) { if (b !== box) b.checked = false; });
    if (box.checked) {
      document.querySelectorAll('input.pick-' + other).forEach(function (b) {
        if (b.dataset.v === box.dataset.v) b.checked = false;
      });
    }
    var chosen = function (c) {  // the variable ticked in column c, or '' if none is ticked
      var b = document.querySelector('input.pick-' + c + ':checked');
      return b ? b.dataset.v : '';
    };

    // [Send both choices to R] =======================================
    // The server receives them as input$sel_pair$resp and
    // input$sel_pair$expl.
    // ================================================================
    Shiny.setInputValue('sel_pair', { resp: chosen('resp'), expl: chosen('expl') }, { priority: 'event' });
  }
</script>
```

```{r}
#| context: setup
# [D0. PACKAGES] =====================================================================================================================================
# Every package the app uses, loaded in one place. "context: setup" makes these available to the whole app, including the server part that runs for
# each visitor.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
library(tidyverse)  # ggplot2 (graphs), readr (read_csv() for data_dictionary.csv), and more
library(scales)     # percent(): labels the chi-squared bar chart's y-axis as percentages
library(shiny)      # the web-app framework
library(DT)         # interactive, filterable data tables
```

```{r}
#| context: setup
# [D. SETUP] =========================================================================================================================================
# Runs once when the app starts (shared by all users). Finds the cleaned .rds files and defines every helper function the app needs. (The packages are
# loaded just above, in [D0].)
# ====================================================================================================================================================

# [D1. Settings] =====================================================================================================================================
# Search for [D1]...[D9] to jump between the parts of this setup section.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
DATA_DIR   <- "Data"   # folder holding the cleaned .rds files
MAX_LEVELS <- 30       # text variables with MORE distinct values are hidden from the picker
TOP_LEVELS <- 10       # analyses keep the 10 most common groups; the rest become "Other"
ALPHA      <- 0.05     # significance level used in the written conclusions

# [D2. Find the cleaned tables] ======================================================================================================================
# Every .rds in Data/ is one table. Files ending in "_combined" are the "Combined" tables; everything else is "Individual". (data_dictionary.csv is
# not an .rds, so it is never mistaken for a table.)
# ====================================================================================================================================================
rds_files       <- list.files(DATA_DIR, pattern = "\\.rds$")
all_keys        <- sub("\\.rds$", "", rds_files)
combined_keys   <- all_keys[grepl("_combined$", all_keys)]
individual_keys <- setdiff(all_keys, combined_keys)

# [D3. Table order and display names] ================================================================================================================
# Show tables in the same order as the Tiny Earth database; anything not in this list is placed at the end (alphabetical).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
preferred_order <- c("institutions", "samples", "dilutions", "library_collections",
                     "aa_screen_libraries", "isolates", "streaks", "aa_screen_isolates",
                     "gram_stains", "other_tests", "rrna_analyses", "antibio_suscepts",
                     "eukaryotics", "extracts", "aa_screen_extracts")

# [sort_keys()] ======================================================================================================================================
# Puts table names in the preferred order; tables not in the list go last, alphabetically. '_combined' is dropped first so a combined table sorts
# right beside its individual version. match() = position in preferred_order; nomatch = 99 sends unknown tables to the end.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
sort_keys <- function(keys) {
  base <- sub("_combined$", "", keys)
  keys[order(match(base, preferred_order, nomatch = 99L), keys)]
}
individual_keys <- sort_keys(individual_keys)  # apply the ordering to both groups of tables
combined_keys   <- sort_keys(combined_keys)

# [pretty_name()] ====================================================================================================================================
# "antibio_suscepts_combined" -> "Antibio Suscepts" (label shown to students)
# ====================================================================================================================================================
pretty_name <- function(key) tools::toTitleCase(gsub("_", " ", sub("_combined$", "", key)))

# [D4. Load a table (once), then remember it] ========================================================================================================
# `table_cache` is shared by all users, so each file is read from disk only the first time anyone opens it. readRDS() returns the table exactly as
# Data_Clean saved it, with every column type intact.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
table_cache <- new.env()  # acts like a shared lookup list: name of table -> data frame
load_table <- function(key) {  # load_table('isolates') returns that table, reading its file once
  if (!exists(key, envir = table_cache, inherits = FALSE)) {  # not cached yet? read it from disk
    path <- file.path(DATA_DIR, paste0(key, ".rds"))
    df   <- readRDS(path)                                # read the table, types intact
    assign(key, as.data.frame(df), envir = table_cache)  # plain data.frame: what DT/stats expect
  }
  get(key, envir = table_cache, inherits = FALSE)  # return the cached copy
}

# [D5. Variable descriptions (the "Description" directory)] ==========================================================================================
# OPTIONAL file: Data/data_dictionary.csv with 3 columns:
#   table, variable, description
# Whatever you write there is shown in the Variable Directory. We start with an empty dictionary so the app still works when the file is missing.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
dictionary <- data.frame(table = character(), variable = character(), description = character())
dict_path  <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "data_dictionary.csv")
if (file.exists(dict_path)) {  # if the file exists, read it with every column as text ('c')
  dictionary <- as.data.frame(read_csv(dict_path, col_types = cols(.default = "c"),
                                       progress = FALSE))
}

# [lookup_description()] =============================================================================================================================
# Finds the description for one variable. Order of search:
#   Rule 1. same table + same variable name
#   Rule 2. same variable name in any table
#   Rule 3. columns joined in from the samples table start with "sample_", so look them up there without the prefix
#   Rule 4. same idea for "institution_" columns and the institutions table
# Nothing found: show a reminder instead of a blank. Dictionary entries use the plain table name, so '_combined' is dropped first.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
lookup_description <- function(key, var) {
  tbl  <- sub("_combined$", "", key)
  # [pick()] =========================================================================================================================================
  # The first non-blank description in a vector, or NA if there is none.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  pick <- function(d) { d <- d[!is.na(d) & nzchar(d)]; if (length(d)) d[1] else NA_character_ }
  out  <- pick(dictionary$description[dictionary$table == tbl & dictionary$variable == var])
  if (is.na(out)) out <- pick(dictionary$description[dictionary$variable == var])
  if (is.na(out) && grepl("^sample_", var))
    out <- pick(dictionary$description[dictionary$table == "samples" & dictionary$variable == sub("^sample_", "", var)])
  if (is.na(out) && grepl("^institution_", var))
    out <- pick(dictionary$description[dictionary$table == "institutions" & dictionary$variable == sub("^institution_", "", var)])
  if (is.na(out)) "(not yet documented - add it to Data/data_dictionary.csv)" else out
}

# [D6. Variable types and test choice] ===============================================================================================================
# Quantitative = numbers. Qualitative = categories (text or TRUE/FALSE). These two types decide which test is run. In var_type(), dates are excluded
# from analysis; numbers (including counts) are Quantitative; everything else (text, TRUE/FALSE) is Qualitative.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
var_type <- function(x) {
  if (inherits(x, c("Date", "POSIXct"))) "Date"
  else if (is.numeric(x))                "Quantitative"
  else                                   "Qualitative"
}

# [pick_test()] ======================================================================================================================================
# Which of the three tests fits a Response / Explanatory pair?
#   quantitative response + qualitative explanatory   -> ANOVA
#   quantitative response + quantitative explanatory  -> simple linear regression
#   qualitative  response + qualitative  explanatory  -> chi-squared test
# Qualitative response + quantitative explanatory has no test in this app, so it returns NA.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
pick_test <- function(resp_type, expl_type) {
  if      (resp_type == "Quantitative" && expl_type == "Qualitative")  "anova"
  else if (resp_type == "Quantitative" && expl_type == "Quantitative") "regression"
  else if (resp_type == "Qualitative"  && expl_type == "Qualitative")  "chisq"
  else NA_character_
}

# [describe_type()] ==================================================================================================================================
# A more detailed label, used only in the Type column of the Variable Directory. ID columns only link tables together, so they are labelled that way
# to stop students analysing them. Text with a huge number of different values is flagged (the picker hides these).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
describe_type <- function(name, x) {
  if (name == "id" || grepl("_id$", name)) return("ID (row link)")
  t <- var_type(x)
  if (t == "Qualitative" && length(unique(stats::na.omit(x))) > MAX_LEVELS) return("Text (many values)")
  t
}

# [analysis_vars()] ==================================================================================================================================
# Which columns of a table are sensible to analyse? We drop ID columns, dates, constant columns, and text columns with too many different values (a
# chi-squared table with hundreds of rows is unreadable).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
analysis_vars <- function(df) {
  keep <- vapply(names(df), function(v) {  # one TRUE/FALSE per column: offer it in the picker?
    x <- df[[v]]
    if (v == "id" || grepl("_id$", v))      return(FALSE)       # drop ID columns
    if (var_type(x) == "Date")              return(FALSE)       # drop dates
    n_unique <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(x)))               # distinct non-missing values
    if (n_unique < 2)                       return(FALSE)       # 0 or 1 values: nothing to compare
    if (!is.numeric(x) && n_unique > MAX_LEVELS) return(FALSE)  # text with too many categories
    TRUE
  }, logical(1))
  names(df)[keep]  # the names of the columns that were kept
}

# [lump_levels()] ====================================================================================================================================
# Keeps the TOP_LEVELS most common categories and lumps the rest into "Other".
# ====================================================================================================================================================
lump_levels <- function(x, top = TOP_LEVELS) {
  x      <- as.character(x)                    # text, so all value types behave the same
  counts <- sort(table(x), decreasing = TRUE)  # count each category, most common first
  if (length(counts) > top) {                  # only lump when there are more than the limit
    keep <- names(counts)[seq_len(top)]       # the names of the most common categories
    x[!is.na(x) & !(x %in% keep)] <- "Other"  # everything else -> 'Other' (NA stays NA)
  }
  factor(x)  # return a factor (R's type for categories)
}

# [D7. Formatting, table and graph helpers] ==========================================================================================================
# fmt_p()  a p-value as text: blank if missing, '< 0.0001' if tiny, otherwise 4 decimals
# fmt_n()  a number as text with d decimals (default 3)
# ====================================================================================================================================================
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p < 0.0001, "< 0.0001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 4)))
fmt_n <- function(x, d = 3) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)

# [html_table()] =====================================================================================================================================
# Turns a data.frame into a tidy HTML table (used in the results page). fmt_col() formats one column: numbers are rounded to 3 decimals with thousands
# commas and NA shown blank; anything else is shown as text. The HTML is an optional caption, then a <table> with a header row and one row per data
# row.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
html_table <- function(df, caption = NULL) {
  fmt_col <- function(col) {
    if (is.numeric(col)) {
      out <- format(round(col, 3), trim = TRUE, scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",")
      out[is.na(col)] <- ""
    } else {
      out <- as.character(col); out[is.na(out)] <- ""
    }
    out
  }
  df[] <- lapply(df, fmt_col)  # apply fmt_col to every column (df[] keeps the data.frame shape)
  tags$div(class = "tbl-wrap",
    if (!is.null(caption)) tags$div(class = "tbl-cap", caption),
    tags$table(class = "te-table",
      tags$thead(tags$tr(lapply(names(df), tags$th))),
      tags$tbody(lapply(seq_len(nrow(df)), function(i) tags$tr(lapply(df[i, ], tags$td))))))
}

# [Graph theme + sea-green -> cyan colour ramp] ======================================================================================================
# te_cols(n)  n colours blending from sea green to cyan (used to colour groups in graphs)
# te_theme()  the common graph look (clean white background, bold green title)
# ====================================================================================================================================================
te_cols  <- function(n) grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#2E8B57", "#20B2AA", "#00BCD4"))(max(n, 1))
te_theme <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1B5E4B"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          legend.position = "right")
}

# [Diagnostic graphs shared by ANOVA and regression] =================================================================================================
# qq_plot()     Q-Q plot: if the residuals are normal, the points follow the line.
# resid_plot()  Residuals vs. fitted values, with a dashed line at 0. ANOVA fitted values repeat for each group, so jitter spreads the points sideways
#               (width = 3% of the fitted-value range, with a fallback value if the range is 0); regression uses plain points. Labels and the theme
#               are added last, then the plot is returned.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
qq_plot <- function(res, title = "Normal Q-Q Plot of Residuals") {
  ggplot(data.frame(r = res), aes(sample = r)) +
    stat_qq(colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = .6) + stat_qq_line(colour = "#2E8B57", linewidth = 1) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles (Residuals)") + te_theme()
}
resid_plot <- function(fitted, res, jitter = FALSE) {
  w <- 0.03 * diff(range(fitted)); if (!is.finite(w) || w == 0) w <- 0.01
  p <- ggplot(data.frame(f = fitted, r = res), aes(f, r)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#1B5E4B")
  p <- p + if (jitter) geom_jitter(width = w, height = 0, colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = .45)
           else        geom_point(colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = .45)
  p + labs(title = "Residuals vs. Fitted Values", x = "Fitted Values", y = "Residuals") + te_theme()
}

safe_shapiro <- function(x) {  # Shapiro-Wilk normality test that never crashes (3-5000 values only)
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]                                     # remove missing and infinite values
  if (length(x) > 5000) { set.seed(1); x <- sample(x, 5000) }  # max 5000: reproducible sample
  tryCatch(stats::shapiro.test(x), error = function(e) NULL)    # NULL if the test can't run
}

# [interp()] =========================================================================================================================================
# Plain-English reading of a diagnostic p-value (p at or above ALPHA = no evidence the assumption is broken).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
interp <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "Could not be computed",
                      ifelse(p >= ALPHA, "No evidence of a violation", "Possible violation - interpret with caution"))

# [conclusion_ui()] ==================================================================================================================================
# Written conclusion shown under each test: reject_txt is shown when p < ALPHA, fail_txt when it is not. The sentence is chosen by: p missing / reject
# H0 (p < ALPHA) / fail to reject H0. Subscript zero is written as a Unicode escape.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
conclusion_ui <- function(p, reject_txt, fail_txt) {
  txt <- if (is.na(p)) "The p-value could not be computed."
         else if (p < ALPHA) sprintf("The p-value (%s) is less than %.2f, so we reject H\u2080. %s", fmt_p(p), ALPHA, reject_txt)
         else sprintf("The p-value (%s) is not less than %.2f, so we fail to reject H\u2080. %s", fmt_p(p), ALPHA, fail_txt)
  tags$p(class = "concl", tags$strong(sprintf("Conclusion (\u03b1 = %.2f): ", ALPHA)), txt)
}

# [D8. DESIGNER SECTION (statistics)] ================================================================================================================
# Per the project plan, the statistics code and the test explanations are meant to be written/owned by the project designer. What follows is a
# working, plain-R starting point: one analysis function per test, plus the explanation text. Replace or rewrite any of it - the rest of the app only
# needs each function to return the same named list (see ANOVA below).
# ====================================================================================================================================================

# [1. ANOVA: quantitative response + qualitative explanatory] ========================================================================================
# yvar = quantitative response column name; gvar = qualitative grouping column name. Returns a named list (type, title, main_plot, summary_ui,
# test_ui, diag_plots, diag_ui): the 'contract' the results page expects from every analyse_* function.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
analyse_anova <- function(df, yvar, gvar) {
  n_orig <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(df[[gvar]])))         # group count before lumping
  d <- data.frame(y = df[[yvar]], g = lump_levels(df[[gvar]]))  # y = the numbers, g = the group
  d <- d[stats::complete.cases(d), ]                            # keep rows where both values exist
  d <- d[d$g %in% names(which(table(d$g) >= 2)), ]              # a group needs 2+ values for spread
  d$g <- droplevels(d$g)                                        # forget group labels with no rows
  validate(need(nlevels(d$g) >= 2 && nrow(d) > nlevels(d$g),    # friendly message if it can't run
                "ANOVA needs at least two groups that each have 2 or more observations."))

  fit  <- stats::aov(y ~ g, data = d)  # fit the ANOVA model: y explained by group
  tab  <- summary(fit)[[1]]            # the ANOVA table as a data frame
  pval <- tab$`Pr(>F)`[1]              # p-value of the F-test
  res  <- stats::resid(fit)            # residuals (each value minus its group mean)

  # [Graph] ==========================================================================================================================================
  # Boxplots + (thinned) raw points + white diamond = group mean.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  pts  <- if (nrow(d) > 4000) d[sample(nrow(d), 4000), ] else d
  main_plot <- ggplot(d, aes(g, y, fill = g)) +
    geom_boxplot(alpha = .55, outlier.shape = NA) +
    geom_jitter(data = pts, width = .15, alpha = .25, size = .8, colour = "#1B5E4B") +
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 3, fill = "white") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = te_cols(nlevels(d$g))) + guides(fill = "none") +
    labs(title = paste(yvar, "by", gvar), x = gvar, y = yvar,
         caption = "White diamond = group mean") + te_theme() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))

  # [Numerical summary by group] =====================================================================================================================
  # One row per group: n, mean, sd, median, min, max. A note is only shown when groups were lumped into 'Other'.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  by_g <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d$y, d$g), function(v)
    data.frame(n = length(v), mean = mean(v), sd = stats::sd(v), median = stats::median(v),
               min = min(v), max = max(v))))
  by_g <- cbind(Group = rownames(by_g), by_g)  # put the group names into their own column
  note <- NULL
  if (n_orig > TOP_LEVELS) note <- sprintf("%s has %d different values; only the %d most common are kept and the rest are grouped as \"Other\".", gvar, n_orig, TOP_LEVELS)

  # [ANOVA table + diagnostic tests] =================================================================================================================
  # Shapiro-Wilk asks: are the residuals normal? An ANOVA on each value's distance from its group median is the Brown-Forsythe test (Levene using
  # medians): do the groups have equal spread?
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  anova_tbl <- data.frame(Source = c("Between groups", "Within groups (Residuals)"),
                          Df = tab$Df, `Sum Sq` = tab$`Sum Sq`, `Mean Sq` = tab$`Mean Sq`,
                          `F value` = c(tab$`F value`[1], NA), `p-value` = c(fmt_p(pval), ""),
                          check.names = FALSE)
  sw  <- safe_shapiro(res)                                      # Shapiro-Wilk
  z   <- abs(d$y - stats::ave(d$y, d$g, FUN = stats::median))  # distances from group medians
  bf  <- stats::anova(stats::lm(z ~ d$g))                       # Brown-Forsythe test
  diag_tbl <- data.frame(  # table of the two assumption checks, each with a plain-English reading
    Test = c("Shapiro-Wilk (residuals are normal)", "Brown-Forsythe / Levene (equal variances)"),
    Statistic = c(if (is.null(sw)) NA else unname(sw$statistic), bf$`F value`[1]),
    `p-value` = fmt_p(c(if (is.null(sw)) NA else sw$p.value, bf$`Pr(>F)`[1])),
    Interpretation = interp(c(if (is.null(sw)) NA else sw$p.value, bf$`Pr(>F)`[1])),
    check.names = FALSE)

  list(type = "anova", title = paste("ANOVA:", yvar, "by", gvar),
       main_plot = main_plot,
       summary_ui = tagList(html_table(by_g, paste("Summary of", yvar, "for each", gvar, "group")),
                            if (!is.null(note)) tags$p(class = "note", note)),
       test_ui = tagList(html_table(anova_tbl, "ANOVA table"),
                         conclusion_ui(pval, "At least one group mean differs from the others.",
                                       "There is not enough evidence that any group mean differs.")),
       diag_plots = list(qq_plot(res), resid_plot(stats::fitted(fit), res, jitter = TRUE)),
       diag_ui = tagList(html_table(diag_tbl, "Assumption checks"),
                         tags$p(class = "note", "With very large samples these tests flag tiny, unimportant departures - judge the plots too.")))
}

# [2. Simple linear regression: quantitative + quantitative] =========================================================================================
# yvar = response column name; xvar = explanatory column name (both quantitative). Returns the same named list as analyse_anova().
# ====================================================================================================================================================
analyse_regression <- function(df, yvar, xvar) {
  d <- data.frame(y = df[[yvar]], x = df[[xvar]])  # working table: y = response, x = explanatory
  d <- d[stats::complete.cases(d), ]
  validate(need(nrow(d) >= 3 && stats::sd(d$x) > 0 && stats::sd(d$y) > 0,  # 3+ rows, both vary
                "Regression needs at least 3 complete observations where both variables vary."))
  fit <- stats::lm(y ~ x, data = d)  # fit the straight-line model
  s   <- summary(fit)                # summary of the fit: coefficients, R-squared, F-statistic
  cf  <- s$coefficients              # coefficient table (estimate, std. error, t, p)
  ci  <- stats::confint(fit)         # 95% confidence intervals for the coefficients
  res <- stats::resid(fit)           # residuals (observed minus predicted)
  # [Overall F-test] =================================================================================================================================
  # p-value of the overall F-test.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  fp  <- stats::pf(s$fstatistic[1], s$fstatistic[2], s$fstatistic[3], lower.tail = FALSE)

  # [Graph] ==========================================================================================================================================
  # Scatterplot (fainter when there are many points) with the least-squares line and its confidence band.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  main_plot <- ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(colour = "#20B2AA", alpha = if (nrow(d) > 500) .3 else .6) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "#2E8B57", fill = "#00BCD4", alpha = .25) +
    labs(title = paste(yvar, "vs.", xvar), x = xvar, y = yvar,
         caption = "Line = least-squares fit; band = 95% confidence interval for the mean") + te_theme()

  desc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(yvar, xvar), function(nm) {  # descriptive stats, both variables
    v <- d[[if (nm == yvar) "y" else "x"]]
    data.frame(Variable = paste0(nm, if (nm == yvar) " (response)" else " (explanatory)"),
               n = length(v), mean = mean(v), sd = stats::sd(v), median = stats::median(v),
               min = min(v), max = max(v))
  }))

  # [Fit, coefficient and assumption tables] =========================================================================================================
  # fit_tbl   strength of the fit: correlation, R-squared, adjusted R-squared, residual standard error
  # coef_tbl  coefficient table for display (Greek letters are written as Unicode escapes)
  # sw        Shapiro-Wilk: are the residuals normal?
  # sp        Spearman correlation of |residuals| with fitted values: near 0 means the spread is constant
  # diag_tbl  the two assumption checks, each with a plain-English reading
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  fit_tbl <- data.frame(Statistic = c("Correlation (r)", "R\u00b2", "Adjusted R\u00b2", "Residual standard error"),
                        Value = c(stats::cor(d$x, d$y), s$r.squared, s$adj.r.squared, s$sigma))
  coef_tbl <- data.frame(Term = c("Intercept (\u03b2\u2080)", paste0("Slope (\u03b2\u2081): ", xvar)),
                         Estimate = cf[, 1], `Std. Error` = cf[, 2], `t value` = cf[, 3],
                         `p-value` = fmt_p(cf[, 4]), `95% CI Lower` = ci[, 1], `95% CI Upper` = ci[, 2],
                         check.names = FALSE)
  sw <- safe_shapiro(res)
  sp <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(abs(res), stats::fitted(fit), method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)),
                 error = function(e) NULL)
  diag_tbl <- data.frame(
    Test = c("Shapiro-Wilk (residuals are normal)", "Spearman: |residuals| vs fitted (constant spread)"),
    Statistic = c(if (is.null(sw)) NA else unname(sw$statistic), if (is.null(sp)) NA else unname(sp$estimate)),
    `p-value` = fmt_p(c(if (is.null(sw)) NA else sw$p.value, if (is.null(sp)) NA else sp$p.value)),
    Interpretation = interp(c(if (is.null(sw)) NA else sw$p.value, if (is.null(sp)) NA else sp$p.value)),
    check.names = FALSE)

  list(type = "regression", title = paste("Simple Linear Regression:", yvar, "on", xvar),
       main_plot = main_plot,
       summary_ui = tagList(html_table(desc, "Descriptive statistics"), html_table(fit_tbl, "Strength of the linear relationship")),
       test_ui = tagList(html_table(coef_tbl, "Regression coefficients"),
                         tags$p(sprintf("Overall model F-test: F = %s on %d and %d df, p-value %s",
                                        fmt_n(s$fstatistic[1]), s$fstatistic[2], s$fstatistic[3], fmt_p(fp))),
                         conclusion_ui(cf[2, 4], "There is evidence of a linear relationship between the two variables.",
                                       "There is not enough evidence of a linear relationship.")),
       diag_plots = list(resid_plot(stats::fitted(fit), res), qq_plot(res)),
       diag_ui = tagList(html_table(diag_tbl, "Assumption checks"),
                         tags$p(class = "note", "Also check the Residuals vs. Fitted plot: a random cloud around 0 supports linearity and equal spread.")))
}

# [3. Chi-squared test of independence: qualitative + qualitative] ===================================================================================
# v1 = ROW variable (the app passes the explanatory variable); v2 = COLUMN variable (the response). Both qualitative. Returns the same named list as
# analyse_anova(). n1 and n2 count each variable's categories before lumping (used for the note below). In the working table d, a = first variable and
# b = second (rare categories lumped into 'Other').
# ====================================================================================================================================================
analyse_chisq <- function(df, v1, v2) {
  n1 <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(df[[v1]]))); n2 <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(df[[v2]])))
  d  <- data.frame(a = lump_levels(df[[v1]]), b = lump_levels(df[[v2]]))
  n_all <- nrow(d)                                  # every row in the table
  d  <- d[stats::complete.cases(d), ]               # only rows where BOTH variables are filled in
  d$a <- droplevels(d$a); d$b <- droplevels(d$b)    # forget category labels with no rows left
  if (nlevels(d$a) < 2 || nlevels(d$b) < 2 || nrow(d) == 0) {
    # [Explain WHY] ==================================================================================================================================
    # A variable can look varied on its own yet be left with one category once the rows where the other variable is blank are removed (e.g. soil_type
    # is only filled in for soil samples).
    # ================================================================================================================================================
    left <- function(f, nm) if (nlevels(f) == 1) sprintf("%s has only one category (\"%s\")", nm, levels(f))
                            else sprintf("%s has %d categories", nm, nlevels(f))
    validate(need(FALSE, sprintf(
      "The chi-squared test needs at least two categories in each variable, using only rows where both are filled in. Only %s of %s rows have both %s and %s filled in; among those rows, %s and %s.",
      format(nrow(d), big.mark = ","), format(n_all, big.mark = ","), v1, v2, left(d$a, v1), left(d$b, v2))))
  }

  # [Run the test] ===================================================================================================================================
  # Contingency table (the count for every combination of categories), then the test with no continuity correction. Small-count warnings are reported
  # by our own check below.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  tab  <- table(d$a, d$b)
  test <- suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(tab, correct = FALSE))
  expd <- test$expected   # counts we would expect if the variables were independent
  low  <- sum(expd < 5)   # how many cells have an expected count below 5
  n    <- sum(tab)        # total sample size
  cv   <- sqrt(unname(test$statistic) / (n * min(nrow(tab) - 1, ncol(tab) - 1)))   # Cramer's V
  note <- NULL            # a note is only shown when categories were lumped into 'Other'
  if (max(n1, n2) > TOP_LEVELS) note <- sprintf("Variables with more than %d categories keep only their %d most common; the rest are grouped as \"Other\".", TOP_LEVELS, TOP_LEVELS)

  # [Graph] ==========================================================================================================================================
  # Stacked 100% bars; each bar is one category of v1, split by v2.
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  plot_df <- as.data.frame(tab, stringsAsFactors = FALSE); names(plot_df) <- c("a", "b", "n")
  main_plot <- ggplot(plot_df, aes(a, n, fill = b)) +
    geom_col(position = "fill", colour = "white") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = te_cols(nlevels(d$b))) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = percent) +
    labs(title = paste(v2, "within each", v1), x = v1, y = "Percent of row", fill = v2) + te_theme() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1))

  with_margins <- as.data.frame.matrix(stats::addmargins(tab))              # with row/column totals
  counts_tbl   <- cbind(Level = rownames(with_margins), with_margins)
  pct          <- as.data.frame.matrix(round(100 * prop.table(tab, 1), 1))  # row % (each row = 100)
  pct_tbl      <- cbind(Level = rownames(pct), pct)

  # [Test results and diagnostics] ===================================================================================================================
  # test_tbl  statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, Cramer's V (effect size), n
  # mc        optional note with a Monte Carlo (simulation-based) p-value, used when many expected counts are small
  # exp_tbl   expected counts, formatted for display
  # sres_tbl  standardized residuals: how strongly each cell departs from independence (beyond about 2 = a lot)
  # heat_df   the residuals reshaped into one row per cell so ggplot can draw them as a heat map (the diagnostic graph)
  # ==================================================================================================================================================
  test_tbl <- data.frame(Statistic = c("Chi-squared (\u03c7\u00b2)", "Degrees of freedom", "p-value", "Cram\u00e9r's V (effect size, 0-1)", "Sample size (n)"),
                         Value = c(fmt_n(test$statistic), as.character(test$parameter), fmt_p(test$p.value), fmt_n(cv), as.character(n)))
  mc <- NULL
  if (low / length(expd) > 0.2) {  # many small expected counts: add a simulation-based p-value
    set.seed(1)
    mcp <- stats::chisq.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 5000)$p.value
    mc  <- tags$p(class = "note", sprintf("Because %d%% of cells have an expected count below 5, a simulation-based (Monte Carlo) p-value is also given: %s.", round(100 * low / length(expd)), fmt_p(mcp)))
  }
  exp_df  <- as.data.frame.matrix(round(expd, 2));  exp_tbl <- cbind(Level = rownames(exp_df), exp_df)
  sres_m  <- test$stdres
  sres_df <- as.data.frame.matrix(round(sres_m, 2)); sres_tbl <- cbind(Level = rownames(sres_df), sres_df)
  heat_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(sres_m), stringsAsFactors = FALSE); names(heat_df) <- c("a", "b", "z")
  heat <- ggplot(heat_df, aes(b, a, fill = z)) + geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = round(z, 1)), size = 3.2) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#00ACC1", mid = "white", high = "#2E8B57", midpoint = 0, name = "Std.\nresidual") +
    labs(title = "Standardized Residuals", x = v2, y = v1) + te_theme() +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1), panel.grid = element_blank())

  list(type = "chisq", title = paste("Chi-squared Test of Independence:", v1, "and", v2),
       main_plot = main_plot,
       summary_ui = tagList(html_table(counts_tbl, sprintf("Counts (rows: %s; columns: %s)", v1, v2)),
                            html_table(pct_tbl, "Row percentages (each row adds to 100%)"),
                            if (!is.null(note)) tags$p(class = "note", note)),
       test_ui = tagList(html_table(test_tbl, "Chi-squared test"), mc,
                         conclusion_ui(test$p.value, "The two variables appear to be associated.",
                                       "There is not enough evidence that the variables are associated.")),
       diag_plots = list(heat),
       diag_ui = tagList(
         tags$p(sprintf("Cells with expected count below 5: %d of %d (%.0f%%). Smallest expected count: %s.",
                        low, length(expd), 100 * low / length(expd), fmt_n(min(expd), 2))),
         tags$p(class = "note", "Rule of thumb: all expected counts should be at least 1, and at least 80% should be 5 or more."),
         html_table(exp_tbl, "Expected counts (if the variables were independent)"),
         html_table(sres_tbl, "Standardized residuals (beyond about \u00b12 = cell contributes strongly)")))
}

# [Explanations (shown under "View More on Test" and in "Learn More")] ===============================================================================
# test_info: the text for each test (name, when it is used, purpose, equations, hypotheses, assumptions). Edit it here to change what 'View More on
# Test' and 'Learn More' show. \uXXXX codes are Unicode symbols (Greek letters, subscripts).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
test_info <- list(
  anova = list(
    name = "Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)",
    when = "One quantitative response variable and one qualitative explanatory variable.",
    purpose = "ANOVA asks whether the average of a quantitative variable differs between the groups (levels) of a categorical variable, by comparing how much the group means vary from each other to how much individual values vary within each group.",
    model = c("y\u1d62\u2c7c = \u03bc + \u03c4\u1d62 + \u03b5\u1d62\u2c7c,   \u03b5\u1d62\u2c7c ~ N(0, \u03c3\u00b2)",
              "y\u1d62\u2c7c = observation j in group i;  \u03bc = overall mean;  \u03c4\u1d62 = effect of group i;  \u03b5\u1d62\u2c7c = random error",
              "F = MSG / MSE = (between-group variation) / (within-group variation)"),
    hypotheses = c("H\u2080: \u03bc\u2081 = \u03bc\u2082 = \u2026 = \u03bc\u2096  (all group means are equal)", "H\u2090: at least one group mean is different"),
    assumptions = "Observations are independent; residuals are approximately normal (Q-Q plot, Shapiro-Wilk); groups have similar spread (residuals vs. fitted, Brown-Forsythe)."),
  regression = list(
    name = "Simple Linear Regression",
    when = "Both variables are quantitative.",
    purpose = "Simple linear regression fits a straight line that describes how the response variable changes, on average, as the explanatory variable increases, and tests whether that relationship is real or could be due to chance.",
    model = c("y\u1d62 = \u03b2\u2080 + \u03b2\u2081x\u1d62 + \u03b5\u1d62,   \u03b5\u1d62 ~ N(0, \u03c3\u00b2)",
              "\u03b2\u2080 = intercept;  \u03b2\u2081 = slope (change in y for each 1-unit increase in x);  \u03b5\u1d62 = random error",
              "t = b\u2081 / SE(b\u2081);   R\u00b2 = proportion of the variation in y explained by x"),
    hypotheses = c("H\u2080: \u03b2\u2081 = 0  (no linear relationship)", "H\u2090: \u03b2\u2081 \u2260 0  (a linear relationship exists)"),
    assumptions = "The relationship is linear; observations are independent; residuals are approximately normal (Q-Q plot, Shapiro-Wilk); residual spread is constant (residuals vs. fitted)."),
  chisq = list(
    name = "Chi-squared Test of Independence",
    when = "Both variables are qualitative (categorical).",
    purpose = "The chi-squared test checks whether two categorical variables are related, by comparing the counts we observed in each combination of categories with the counts we would expect if the variables were unrelated.",
    model = c("E\u1d62\u2c7c = (row total i \u00d7 column total j) / n",
              "\u03c7\u00b2 = \u03a3 (O\u1d62\u2c7c \u2212 E\u1d62\u2c7c)\u00b2 / E\u1d62\u2c7c,   df = (rows \u2212 1)(columns \u2212 1)",
              "O = observed count;  E = expected count if independent"),
    hypotheses = c("H\u2080: the two variables are independent (not associated)", "H\u2090: the two variables are associated"),
    assumptions = "Observations are independent; each observation falls in exactly one cell; expected counts are large enough (all \u2265 1 and at least 80% \u2265 5).")
)

# [info_ui()] ========================================================================================================================================
# Builds the explanation block for one test: when it is used, purpose, mathematical model, hypotheses, and assumptions (diagnostics).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
info_ui <- function(type) {
  i <- test_info[[type]]  # pick the entry for this test
  tagList(
    tags$p(tags$strong("When it is used: "), i$when),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Purpose: "), i$purpose),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Mathematical model:")), lapply(i$model, function(m) tags$div(class = "formula", m)),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Hypotheses:"), style = "margin-top:10px;"), lapply(i$hypotheses, function(m) tags$div(class = "formula", m)),
    tags$p(tags$strong("Assumptions (diagnostics): "), i$assumptions, style = "margin-top:10px;"))
}

# [END DESIGNER SECTION] =============================================================================================================================
# Everything from [D8] down to here is the designer section.
# ====================================================================================================================================================

# [D9. Helpers that build pieces of the page] ========================================================================================================
# selector_item(): one clickable table name in the Table Selector. Clicking sends the table's name to the server as input$pick_table. The selected row
# is highlighted.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
selector_item <- function(key, active) {
  tags$a(href = "#", class = paste("te-item", if (active) "active"),
         onclick = sprintf("Shiny.setInputValue('pick_table', '%s', {priority: 'event'}); return false;", key),
         pretty_name(key))
}

# [selector_details() and selector_section()] ========================================================================================================
# A collapsible section of the selector (click the heading to open / close it). `id` names the section so the server can remember whether it was left
# open, `open` is that remembered state, and `...` is the content inside the section.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
selector_details <- function(id, title, open, ...) {
  tags$details(class = "sel-details", open = if (open) NA,
               ontoggle = sprintf("Shiny.setInputValue('sec_%s', this.open);", id),
               tags$summary(class = "sel-head", title), ...)
}
selector_section <- function(id, title, keys, current, open = TRUE) {
  selector_details(id, title, open,
                   if (length(keys)) lapply(keys, function(k) selector_item(k, k == current))
                   else tags$p(class = "hint", "No tables found."))
}

# [pick_row()] =======================================================================================================================================
# One row of the variable picker: the variable name, then a checkbox in the Response column and a checkbox in the Explanatory column. Ticking calls
# tePick() (JavaScript above). In box(), data-v holds the variable name for tePick(), and 'checked' restores an earlier tick.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
pick_row <- function(v, type, is_resp, is_expl) {
  box <- function(col, on) tags$input(type = "checkbox", class = paste0("pick-", col), `data-v` = v,
                                      checked = if (on) NA, onclick = sprintf("tePick('%s', this);", col))
  div(class = "pick-row",
      span(class = "pick-name", v, span(class = "vtype", paste0("(", type, ")"))),
      box("resp", is_resp), box("expl", is_expl))
}
```

```{r}
# [E. PAGE SHELL (rendered once)] ====================================================================================================================
# Everything inside "page" is filled in by the server section below.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
tagList(
  div(class = "te-banner",
      h1("Tiny Earth Project \u2013 Bio 181 Lab"),
      p("Explore soil-bacteria data from the Tiny Earth network and test relationships between variables \u00b7 BYU-Idaho")),
  uiOutput("page"))  # placeholder: see output$page in the server section [F2]
```

```{r}
#| context: server
# [F. SERVER] ========================================================================================================================================
# Runs separately for EACH visitor, so one student's clicks never affect another student's session.
# ====================================================================================================================================================

# [F1. This visitor's app state] =====================================================================================================================
#   page     : "viewer" (data viewer) or "results" (analysis page)
#   mode     : "browse" (table selector) or "select" (pick two variables)
#   view     : "table" (Table Viewer) or "description" (Variable Directory)
#   table    : the table currently selected
#   resp     : the variable ticked in the Response column ("" = none yet)
#   expl     : the variable ticked in the Explanatory column ("" = none yet)
#   analysis : the table + response + explanatory variable sent to the results page
# ====================================================================================================================================================
rv <- reactiveValues(page = "viewer", mode = "browse", view = "table",
                     table = if (length(individual_keys)) individual_keys[1] else all_keys[1],
                     resp = "", expl = "", analysis = NULL)

# [current_df() and table_label()] ===================================================================================================================
# current_df()   the data frame of the selected table. A reactive re-runs by itself whenever rv$table changes.
# table_label()  text such as 'Samples (Individual)' used in headings.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
current_df   <- reactive({ req(rv$table); load_table(rv$table) })
table_label  <- reactive({ req(rv$table); paste0(pretty_name(rv$table), if (grepl("_combined$", rv$table)) " (Combined)" else " (Individual)") })

# [F2. Which page is showing] ========================================================================================================================
# No .rds files found: show instructions instead of the app. Viewer: selector / picker card on the left (left_ui), table card on the right (right_ui).
# Otherwise show the analysis page.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
output$page <- renderUI({
  if (length(all_keys) == 0)
    return(div(class = "panel-card", h4("No data found"),
               p("The Data folder has no .rds files yet. Run the Data_Clean script first, then restart the app.")))
  if (rv$page == "viewer")
    div(class = "app-grid",
        div(uiOutput("left_ui")),
        div(uiOutput("right_ui")))
  else
    uiOutput("results_ui")
})

# [F3. LEFT PANEL: table selector OR variable picker] ================================================================================================
# browse = Table Selector; select = variable picker (the else branch below).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
output$left_ui <- renderUI({
  if (rv$mode == "browse") {
    # [Table Selector] ===============================================================================================================================
    # Each table section is collapsible. Whether it is open is remembered in input$sec_<id> (isolate() = read it now without re-drawing the panel each
    # time one is toggled). The bottom row holds Description (left) and Run Analysis (right). Description shows / hides the Variable Directory for the
    # selected table; it is filled in (solid green) while that view is open.
    # ================================================================================================================================================
    is_open <- function(id) { v <- isolate(input[[paste0("sec_", id)]]); is.null(v) || isTRUE(v) }
    div(class = "panel-card left-card",
        actionButton("btn_background", "Background", class = "btn-te btn-wide"),
        div(class = "selector-scroll",
            div(class = "sel-title", style = "margin-top:10px;", "Table Selector"),
            selector_section("Individual", "Individual", individual_keys, rv$table, is_open("Individual")),
            selector_section("Combined",   "Combined",   combined_keys,   rv$table, is_open("Combined"))),
        div(class = "btn-row",
            actionButton("btn_desc", "Description", title = "Describe every variable in the selected table",
                         class = paste("btn-te", if (rv$view != "description") "btn-outline")),
            actionButton("btn_run", "Run Analysis", class = "btn-te btn-cyan")))
  } else {
    # [Variable picker (same card layout as the selector)] ===========================================================================================
    # Two checkbox columns sit beside every variable: Response (y) and Explanatory (x). isolate() restores earlier ticks without re-drawing the panel
    # on every click.
    # ================================================================================================================================================
    df   <- current_df()
    vars <- analysis_vars(df)  # columns worth analysing (see analysis_vars())
    div(class = "panel-card left-card",
        div(class = "sel-title", "Select two variables"),
        p(class = "hint", paste("Table:", table_label())),
        p(class = "hint", "Tick one Response (y) and one Explanatory (x) variable."),
        div(class = "selector-scroll",
            div(class = "pick-head", span("Variable"), span(class = "h-resp", "Response (y)"), span(class = "h-expl", "Explanatory (x)")),
            lapply(vars, function(v) pick_row(v, var_type(df[[v]]), v == isolate(rv$resp), v == isolate(rv$expl)))),
        uiOutput("sel_status"),
        div(class = "btn-row",
            actionButton("btn_back", "Back", class = "btn-te btn-outline"),
            uiOutput("analyse_btn", inline = TRUE)))
  }
})

# [F4. Variable picker status and Analyse button] ====================================================================================================
# pair_test()          which test fits the ticked pair? NA until both columns have a variable (or if no test fits).
# output$sel_status    message under the variable list: progress, a warning for a pair with no test, or the test that will run. n = how many columns
#                      have a tick (0, 1 or 2).
# output$analyse_btn   "Analyse" is greyed out until a valid Response + Explanatory pair is ticked, then lights up.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
pair_test <- reactive({
  df <- current_df()
  if (!nzchar(rv$resp) || !nzchar(rv$expl)) return(NA_character_)
  pick_test(var_type(df[[rv$resp]]), var_type(df[[rv$expl]]))
})

output$sel_status <- renderUI({
  n <- (nzchar(rv$resp)) + (nzchar(rv$expl))
  if (n < 2)                p(class = "hint", sprintf("%d of 2 selected", n))
  else if (is.na(pair_test())) p(class = "concl", "A qualitative response with a quantitative explanatory variable has no matching test in this app. Swap the columns or choose different variables.")
  else                      p(class = "hint", "Ready: ", tags$strong(test_info[[pair_test()]]$name))
})

output$analyse_btn <- renderUI({
  if (!is.na(pair_test())) actionButton("btn_analyse", "Analyse", class = "btn-te btn-glow")
  else actionButton("btn_analyse", "Analyse", class = "btn-te", disabled = "disabled")
})

# [F5. RIGHT PANEL: Table Viewer OR Variable Directory] ==============================================================================================
# Table Viewer (the data) or Variable Directory (what each column means).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
output$right_ui <- renderUI({
  if (rv$view == "table") {
    div(class = "panel-card",
        div(class = "viewer-head", h3("Table Viewer"),
            span(class = "current", "Currently viewing: ", tags$strong(table_label()))),
        DTOutput("data_table"),  # placeholder for the interactive table in output$data_table below
        div(class = "table-foot", textOutput("table_count")))
  } else {
    div(class = "panel-card",
        div(class = "viewer-head", h3("Variable Directory"),
            span(class = "current", "Table: ", tags$strong(table_label()))),
        DTOutput("dict_table"),
        div(class = "table-foot", "Each row describes one column (factor) of the selected table."))
  }
})

# [output$data_table] ================================================================================================================================
# The data table: filter boxes sit directly above each column, a search box above the table, scroll bars both ways, and "Showing x to y of N entries"
# at the bottom. Long text (e.g. DNA sequences) is shortened in the cell; hover to see all of it. trim_js is JavaScript that DataTables runs on each
# text cell: it cuts text longer than 60 characters and shows the full text as a hover tooltip (esc() makes odd characters safe to show), and defs
# applies it to the text columns only (nothing if there are none). In datatable(), filter = 'top' puts a filter box above each column; scrollX/scrollY
# add scroll bars; dom 'lfrtip' = length menu, search box, table, 'Showing x to y of N' line, page buttons.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
output$data_table <- renderDT({
  df <- current_df()
  text_cols <- unname(which(vapply(df, is.character, logical(1)))) - 1
  trim_js <- JS(r"(function(data, type, row) {
      // Only change what is DRAWN; sorting and searching still use the full text.
      if (type === 'display' && data != null && data.length > 60) {
        // esc(): replace characters that have special meaning in HTML.
        var esc = function(s) { return s.replace(/&/g,'&amp;').replace(/</g,'&lt;').replace(/"/g,'&quot;'); };
        // Shortened text; the title attribute is the hover tooltip.
        return '<span title="' + esc(data) + '">' + esc(data.substr(0, 60)) + '&hellip;</span>';
      }
      // Anything short (or not being displayed) is returned unchanged.
      return data; }
  )")
  defs <- if (length(text_cols)) list(list(targets = text_cols, render = trim_js)) else list()
  datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", selection = "none", class = "stripe hover compact",
            options = list(scrollX = TRUE, scrollY = "52vh", scrollCollapse = TRUE,
                           pageLength = 25, lengthMenu = c(10, 25, 50, 100),
                           dom = "lfrtip", columnDefs = defs))
})
output$table_count <- renderText({  # text under the table: rows (data points) and columns (factors)
  df <- current_df()
  sprintf("%s data points (rows) \u00d7 %d factors (columns) in this table.", format(nrow(df), big.mark = ","), ncol(df))
})

# [output$dict_table: the Variable Directory] ========================================================================================================
# One row per column of the table: name, type, plain-English description, % missing, distinct values, and the first 3 example values. Shown as a
# table; dom 'ftip' = search box, table, info line, page buttons.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
output$dict_table <- renderDT({
  df <- current_df(); key <- rv$table
  info <- data.frame(
    Variable = names(df),
    Type = vapply(names(df), function(v) describe_type(v, df[[v]]), character(1)),
    Description = vapply(names(df), function(v) lookup_description(key, v), character(1)),
    `% Missing` = vapply(df, function(x) round(100 * mean(is.na(x)), 1), numeric(1)),
    `Distinct Values` = vapply(df, function(x) length(unique(stats::na.omit(x))), numeric(1)),
    `Example Values` = vapply(df, function(x) substr(paste(utils::head(unique(as.character(stats::na.omit(x))), 3), collapse = "; "), 1, 70), character(1)),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  datatable(info, rownames = FALSE, selection = "none", class = "stripe hover compact",
            options = list(scrollX = TRUE, scrollY = "52vh", scrollCollapse = TRUE, pageLength = 50, dom = "ftip"))
})

# [F6. Clicks in the viewer] =========================================================================================================================
# Each observeEvent() runs when its button or input changes. The JavaScript tePick() reports which variable is ticked in each column (input$sel_pair).
# btn_run opens the variable picker (fresh); btn_back goes back to the table selector.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
observeEvent(input$pick_table, {                      # chose a different table
  req(input$pick_table %in% all_keys)
  rv$table <- input$pick_table
})
observeEvent(input$btn_desc, {                        # Description: flip table <-> directory
  rv$view <- if (rv$view == "description") "table" else "description"
})
observeEvent(input$btn_run,  { rv$mode <- "select"; rv$resp <- ""; rv$expl <- "" })
observeEvent(input$btn_back, { rv$mode <- "browse"; rv$resp <- ""; rv$expl <- "" })

observeEvent(input$sel_pair, {                       # tePick() reports the ticked pair
  req(rv$page == "viewer", rv$mode == "select")
  rv$resp <- input$sel_pair$resp
  rv$expl <- input$sel_pair$expl
})

observeEvent(input$btn_analyse, {                     # go to the results page
  req(!is.na(pair_test()))
  rv$analysis <- list(table = rv$table, resp = rv$resp, expl = rv$expl)
  rv$page <- "results"
})
observeEvent(input$btn_results_back, { rv$page <- "viewer" })

# [F7. Background window] ============================================================================================================================
# showModal() opens a pop-up window; easyClose lets people click outside it to close. The text inside is ordinary HTML tags and can be edited freely.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
observeEvent(input$btn_background, {
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = "Background", size = "l", easyClose = TRUE, footer = modalButton("Close"),
    h4("What is Tiny Earth?"),
    p("Tiny Earth is a student-sourced antibiotic discovery network led by the University of Wisconsin\u2013Madison. Students at schools around the world collect soil samples, isolate bacteria from them, and test those bacteria for antibiotic activity. The results from many schools are shared in the ",
      tags$a(href = "https://publicdata.tinyearth.wisc.edu/", target = "_blank", "Tiny Earth Public Database"), "."),
    h4("What is this app for?"),
    p("This app helps Bio 181 Lab students at BYU\u2013Idaho explore that public data and get a first taste of biostatistics, bioinformatics, and biological data science. You can browse and filter every table, then pick any two variables and the app chooses the right test for you:"),
    tags$ul(
      tags$li(tags$strong("Quantitative response + qualitative explanatory"), " \u2192 Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)"),
      tags$li(tags$strong("Quantitative + quantitative"), " \u2192 Simple Linear Regression"),
      tags$li(tags$strong("Qualitative + qualitative"), " \u2192 Chi-squared Test of Independence")),
    h4("How to use it"),
    tags$ol(
      tags$li("Pick a table in the Table Selector. Individual tables match the Tiny Earth database; Combined tables add the related sample and institution columns."),
      tags$li("Use the filter boxes above the Table Viewer to search and narrow the data. Use the Description button to see what each column means."),
      tags$li("Press Run Analysis, tick exactly two variables, then press Analyse."),
      tags$li("Read the graph and numerical summary. Open View More on Test for the test, its equations, and diagnostic checks. Learn More explains each test; Save PDF prints the page.")),
    p(class = "note", "All results are intended for academic and learning purposes.")))
})

# [F8. RESULTS PAGE] =================================================================================================================================
# analysis_type()  "anova", "regression" or "chisq", decided by the TYPES of the Response and Explanatory variables chosen in the picker. req() waits
#                  until an analysis has been requested.
# result()         runs the matching test function (from the designer section above).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
analysis_type <- reactive({
  a  <- req(rv$analysis)
  df <- load_table(a$table)  # load the table that was chosen
  pick_test(var_type(df[[a$resp]]), var_type(df[[a$expl]]))
})

result <- reactive({
  a  <- req(rv$analysis)
  df <- load_table(a$table)
  tp <- analysis_type()
  validate(need(!is.na(tp), "No test matches a qualitative response with a quantitative explanatory variable. Go back and swap the columns."))
  switch(tp,
         anova      = analyse_anova(df, yvar = a$resp, gvar = a$expl),
         regression = analyse_regression(df, yvar = a$resp, xvar = a$expl),
         chisq      = analyse_chisq(df, a$expl, a$resp))  # rows = explanatory, columns = response
})

# [Top bar and results body] =========================================================================================================================
# output$results_ui    the top bar (Back / Learn More / Save PDF), built once per analysis. "Save PDF" uses the browser's print window - choose "Save
#                      as PDF" as the printer.
# output$results_body  everything under the top bar. result() is calculated once and shared with the plots; r = the named list returned by the
#                      matching analyse_* function. The "View More on Test" drop-down is a button that toggles the "open" class (see CSS). When
#                      printing, the section is always shown.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
output$results_ui <- renderUI({
  a  <- req(rv$analysis)
  div(class = "panel-card results-page",
      div(class = "results-bar no-print",
          actionButton("btn_results_back", "\u2190 Back to Data", class = "btn-te btn-outline"),
          div(class = "spacer"),
          actionButton("btn_learn", "Learn More", class = "btn-te btn-cyan"),
          tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-te", onclick = "window.print();", "Save PDF")),
      p(class = "hint", paste("Table:", pretty_name(a$table), "\u00b7 Response (y):", a$resp, "\u00b7 Explanatory (x):", a$expl)),
      uiOutput("results_body"))
})

output$results_body <- renderUI({
  r <- result()
  div(
    h2(r$title),
    h3(class = "sec-title", "Graph"),
    plotOutput("res_plot", width = "780px", height = "440px"),
    h3(class = "sec-title", "Numerical Summary"),
    r$summary_ui,
    div(class = "more",
        tags$button(type = "button", class = "btn btn-te more-toggle no-print",
                    onclick = "this.parentNode.classList.toggle('open');", "View More on Test \u25be"),
        div(class = "more-body",
            h3(class = "sec-title", paste("About the Test:", test_info[[r$type]]$name)),
            info_ui(r$type),
            h3(class = "sec-title", "Test Results"), r$test_ui,
            h3(class = "sec-title", "Diagnostics"),
            div(class = "diag-row", lapply(seq_along(r$diag_plots), function(i)
              plotOutput(paste0("diag_plot_", i), width = "520px", height = "360px"))),
            r$diag_ui)))
})

# [Plots] ============================================================================================================================================
# Plots use fixed sizes and suspendWhenHidden = FALSE so they are already drawn when the drop-down is opened or the page is printed. The two
# diagnostic plots are created in a loop; local() gives each pass its own copy of i. req() skips plot 2 for tests that only have one diagnostic plot
# (chi-squared).
# ====================================================================================================================================================
output$res_plot <- renderPlot(result()$main_plot, width = 780, height = 440, res = 110)
outputOptions(output, "res_plot", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
for (i in 1:2) local({
  ii <- i; id <- paste0("diag_plot_", ii)
  output[[id]] <- renderPlot({ r <- result(); req(length(r$diag_plots) >= ii); r$diag_plots[[ii]] },
                             width = 520, height = 360, res = 100)
  outputOptions(output, id, suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
})

# [F9. Learn More window] ============================================================================================================================
# Shows a table of which test goes with which variable types, then one explanation block per test, with the test you just ran first.
# ====================================================================================================================================================
observeEvent(input$btn_learn, {
  current <- analysis_type()
  if (is.na(current)) current <- "anova"
  order   <- c(current, setdiff(names(test_info), current))     # show the test you ran first
  showModal(modalDialog(
    title = "Learn More: The Three Tests", size = "l", easyClose = TRUE, footer = modalButton("Close"),
    p("The app picks the test from the types of the two variables you chose:"),
    tags$table(class = "te-table",
      tags$thead(tags$tr(tags$th("Variables chosen"), tags$th("Test used"))),
      tags$tbody(lapply(names(test_info), function(k) tags$tr(tags$td(test_info[[k]]$when), tags$td(test_info[[k]]$name))))),
    lapply(order, function(k) tagList(h4(class = "sec-title", test_info[[k]]$name), info_ui(k)))))
})
```
